What moves the water · Digital twin: one year, 495 wells

What moves the water?

Two forces drive a borewell's water level: rain slowly refilling the ground, and pumping drawing it down. Over a year the model learned how strong each one is, and how long rain takes to arrive.

Why this matters
  • Knowing that rain takes 1–4 weeks to arrive lets a forecast use rain that has already fallen, so there's no need for a weather forecast.
  • Knowing which wells are most sensitive to pumping shows where cutting back helps most.
Limits
  • The model treats all rain alike. Early showers before the monsoon mostly soak into dry soil, so it tends to over-credit them.
  • One rainfall series is used for the whole city. Local rain gauges and well locations would sharpen this.
Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
